articles.title: Glacier Point Star Party
articles.summary: The article recounts the author's experience at the Glacier Point Star Party, attended by various astronomy clubs and featuring diverse telescopes, including a 24-inch dobsonian. Despite some cloudy conditions, an overcrowded campsite, and an encounter with black bears, the author enjoyed impressive celestial views and plans to attend the event again. The experience highlighted the joy of shared observing and the impact of aperture on astronomical viewing.

articles.title: Changes at Fremont Peak
articles.summary: Fremont Peak State Park is undergoing significant improvements, including new entrance pavement, a potential access gate, and major renovations around the observatory. These upgrades feature new paving, a pedestrian path, a terraced group activity area, and eight powered telescope pads, funded by Volunteer Enhancement Funds. While four trees will be removed and public input was limited, the author anticipates these changes will greatly enhance the park for astronomy enthusiasts despite temporary construction inconvenience.

articles.title: Mooning
articles.summary: The article is divided into two sections: "Mooning" by Dave North, which explains the personal and historical significance behind his website domain "timocharis.com," detailing the lunar crater and the ancient Greek astronomer Timocharis's contributions to early astronomy. The second section, "Deep Sky August" by Mark Wagner, offers a guide for amateur astronomers, highlighting a new observing site (Coyote Lake Park) and providing detailed observations and tips for several deep-sky objects visible in August, including a double star, globular clusters, planetary nebulae, and a supernova remnant.

articles.title: A Letter from the President of the ASP
articles.summary: Alex Filippenko, President of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific (ASP), shares a personal anecdote about his early passion for astronomy and the profound impact of amateur astronomy clubs on his journey. He connects this experience to the ASP's mission of public science education, urging readers to join the society to support programs like Project ASTRO and receive their Mercury magazine. The letter also announces an upcoming public symposium, "The Cosmic Thread: From Stars to Life," co-sponsored with the AANC at UC Berkeley.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar August 2002
articles.summary: This document presents the 'Celestial Calendar' for August 2002, offering essential astronomical data for observers. It details lunar phases, positions and magnitudes for visible planets including Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. Additionally, it provides information on solar data, hours of darkness, astronomical twilight, sidereal time, and highlights the 'Darkest Saturday Night' for optimal viewing conditions.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: This article outlines the current status of the SJAA (San Jose Astronomical Association) loaner telescope program, providing details on scopes available for immediate borrowing, those currently on loan with due dates, and scopes with extended loan periods. It includes contact information for members interested in borrowing equipment and lists individuals on the waiting list for specific telescopes. The program aims to make various astronomical instruments accessible to club members.
